 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. SAINTS head coach Tonda Eckert highlighted that major injury absences have been a problem for Derby County ahead of facing the Rams at St Mary's on Saturday.
 Derby are currently second-bottom in the Championship after a poor start, winning just two of their 15 league matches.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, that second win came last time out, beating Bolton Wanderers 3-1 before the international break.
 John Eustace's side played against Everton in a behind closed doors friendly during the off-period which saw some key players return to the pitch.
 "I think no team can compensate for some key players to be out," Eckert insisted. "I think [Matt] Clarke has been back now. He's played 60 minutes against Everton in the international break. They have [Patrick] Agyemang back.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Not just for the quality on the pitch, but I think if you travel to a game, you just have some key personalities within a group that just make the whole feeling around a group different.
 "I think these two will do that for Derby so I expect them to come very strong. They finished the last game before the break very well. They've gone from a back-four to a back-three.
 "They've continued to play in a back three now in the international break in the friendly.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I think they've had some tough games, a tough spell. That team is so physical, especially if they decide to put another centre-back in right from the start. I think one of the most physical strikers on the pitch.
 Read more:

 "We've seen how much damage he can do to teams, how difficult it is to control him. It will be a tough, tough game for us tomorrow.
 "I hope that with the support at home, we manage to bring the ball on the ground. I think that once we get into a way of playing our football, we have so much quality and we need to make sure we bring that on the pitch."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Saints are looking to return to winning ways after suffering a shock 1-0 defeat at bottom side Preston North End before the international break.
 They have only lost one league game at home this calendar year, dating way back to January against Hull City.
